subject: Re: Dedicated conversion credits & sizing plan
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@neohealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: NeoHealth Procurement <procurement@neohealth.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — migration credits and sizing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time to speak yesterday. As discussed, NeoHealth is evaluating a migration from our current hosted usage on Redwood to a Dedicated GPU pool (private VPC). Before we loop procurement I need a clear mapping of how our existing hosted credits would convert to Dedicated commits and what bridge coverage you can offer while we finalize an annual commit.

Key asks from procurement:
- A conversion-credit schedule: how many months of committed capacity (or % credit) do we receive for X months of hosted consumption/credits.
- Whether commit offsets can be applied retroactively to usage in the same billing month.
- Recommended GPU pool sizing to meet a baseline throughput of ~600 rps (99th percentile latency target ≤ 350ms for most LLM routes).
- Proposed SLA/throughput guarantees and how they change across tiers (standard vs premium).
- Any bridge month proposals (e.g., 1–3 months) where we retain hosted credits while committed capacity ramps.

Procurement timeline is tight — internal approval window is ~2 weeks. Can you send a short written proposal we can attach to the SOW? An estimate workbook (rough commit pricing by GPU type + conversion table) would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sophie Lang
Sr. AI Product Manager
NeoHealth

--
Attachment: N/A
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@neohealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, alex_martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — migration credits and sizing

Hi Sophie — great to meet earlier. I pulled together an initial estimate and a proposed conversion table; attaching the workbook (NeoHealth_Dedicated_Estimate_v3.xlsx). High level summary below so procurement has something concise: 

Summary (short):
- Conversion credits: Standard offer is a 1:1 offset for hosted credits up to first 3 months (effectively 3 bridge months) OR a structured conversion credit of up to 20% of annual commit value if NeoHealth opts for a 12-month reserved commit up front. We can present both options.
- Bridge months: We recommend 2 months of overlap for a smooth traffic cutover; 3 months is possible but we generally reserve 3 months only for strategic, enterprise transitions.
- GPU pool sizing: Based on your stated 600 rps baseline and 99th latency ≤350ms, preliminary sizing points to a 6x A100-ish equivalent pool with autoscaling headroom ~30%. Exact model mix depends on model sequence lengths — workbook has two profiles (short-seq chat vs long-context embedding-heavy).
- SLA: Standard tier includes 99.5% uptime SLA and baseline throughput with soft burst allowances. Premium tier (SLA-backed throughput guarantee) is available at +25% list price; includes dedicated burst buffer and guaranteed KV cache hit ratios.

Next steps: If you can share a 30/60/90-day traffic sample (tokens/minute or requests per second by route), I’ll update the workbook with a recommended pool composition and a firm commit price. For procurement, I can also draft a short proposal paragraph they can attach to the SOW.

Attachment: NeoHealth_Dedicated_Estimate_v3.xlsx (excel workbook, cost model + conversion table)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@neohealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — migration credits and sizing

Karthik — thanks for the quick reply and the workbook. I reviewed the conversion examples and have a few clarifying questions procurement would like answered before we present to legal: 

1) Conversion mechanics: your note about a 1:1 offset up to 3 months vs 20% annual commit credit is helpful. Can you give a precise table: e.g., if we have $240k in hosted credits used in past 12 months, how does that translate to months of Dedicated commit at your proposed pool sizing? Procurement needs a dollar-to-months conversion example they can include in the approval memo.

2) Retroactive offsets: procurement asked if commit offsets can be applied to usage that has already occurred in the same billing month prior to signing. Is this allowed, and if so what is the cutoff date?

3) Throughput guarantee: the team needs language we can pass to infra ops. Specifically: what does the premium throughput SLA commit to (min sustained rps at 99th percentile, and remediation credits if missed)?

4) Pricing floor and discounting: NeoHealth is evaluating a 12–24 month commit. Are there volume discount tiers we can expect at $X/month ranges? We will share expected monthly spend once we finalize sizing.

Procurement also asked whether Redwood can sign a short (1–3 month) bridge addendum that keeps hosted API active while Dedicated capacity ramps and credits are applied. That addendum can sit outside the main MSA but needs to be referenced in the SOW.

I can send the 30/60/90 traffic export tomorrow. Timeline: internal approval meeting next Wed (2026-06-24) so we need final language by EOD Tuesday (2026-06-23) to include in the packet.

Thanks — Sophie

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — migration credits & bridge addendum

Hi Sophie / Karthik — looping in final commercial guidance from our side. I reviewed the workbook and spoke with Finance; below is an explicit proposal NeoHealth can take to procurement/legal.

Commercial proposal (Redwood):
- Conversion credit options (pick one):
  * Option A (Bridge-first): 2 bridge months where hosted credits offset Dedicated commit billing 1:1 for the first two billed months following go-live. This preserves hosted access while capacity ramps.
  * Option B (Commit-conversion): Up to 20% conversion credit applied to the first 12 months of committed spend when NeoHealth signs a 12-month reserved commit at or above the baseline pool in the workbook. The credit is applied as a dollar credit spread evenly across months 1–12.
- Retroactive offsets: We can apply offsets to usage in the same billing month up to the date of signature, provided the customer signs within 10 business days of the invoice date and the usage is verifiable. Retroactive offsets are not standard beyond that window.
- Throughput SLA (Premium tier): guaranteed sustained baseline of 600 rps at 99th percentile ≤ 350ms (for the routes identified in the workbook) with remediation credits equal to 5% of monthly committed spend per SLA miss, capped at 50% monthly. Premium SLA requires a minimum 12-month commit and the pool composition we recommended.
- GPU pool sizing & autoscaling: workbook recommends a 6x A100-equivalent base with autoscale headroom to 8x during 30% traffic spikes. Final sizing will be validated against your 30/60/90 traffic export; we will update commit units accordingly.
- Discount tiers: for 12-month commits, we can offer a 10% list discount at baseline pool; for 24-month commits, 18% discount. Additional strategic credits (one-time) up to 5% available upon executive approval.

Attachments included: SOW template and a short bridge addendum we can insert into the MSA (SOW_azure_pool_sizing.pdf).

If NeoHealth prefers Option A, we consider two bridge months standard; Option B yields a larger conversion credit but requires the upfront commit. We are happy to draft an addendum (1–2 paragraphs) that procurement can attach.

Karthik — happy to review the language with procurement on Tue (2026-06-23) morning if that helps. Sophie — if you can send the traffic export, we’ll lock sizing and a final dollar figure for the commit.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Deals
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_azure_pool_sizing.pdf (pdf, SOW + bridge addendum template)

Subject: Re: Dedicated conversion credits & sizing plan — agreed next steps

Sophie — thanks for the traffic export yesterday and for the good conversation on Tuesday. Per procurement's ask and Marissa's note above, here's the agreed commercial summary for inclusion in the SOW/approval packet:

Agreed commercial terms (summary):
- NeoHealth will commit to a 12-month Dedicated pool equivalent to the baseline in NeoHealth_Dedicated_Estimate_v3.xlsx (6x A100-equivalent) with 30% autoscale headroom.
- Conversion credits: NeoHealth selected Option B (Commit-conversion). Redwood will apply a one-time 20% conversion credit of the annual committed spend, credited as a dollar offset evenly across months 1–12.
- Bridge coverage: Redwood will keep hosted API access open for 2 bridge months post-signature to allow traffic cutover; hosted credits will offset Dedicated billing 1:1 for those two months.
- Retroactive offsets: Redwood will apply offsets to usage in the current billing month up to the date of signature provided NeoHealth signs within 10 business days of invoice issuance (per Marissa's note).
- SLA: Premium throughput SLA confirmed — 600 rps sustained, 99th percentile latency ≤ 350ms; remediation credits as described. Premium SLA activated upon pool provisioning and requires the 12-month commit.
- Pricing/discount: 12-month commit discount applied at 10% off list; the 20% conversion credit is in addition and reflected in month 1–12 invoices.

Next steps (operational):
1) Procurement to confirm SOW language for inclusion; Redwood will provide a short paragraph for the SOW and a bridge addendum (I attached the link to the draft).
2) DocuSign: I'll send the MSA + SOW via DocuSign once procurement confirms the final SOW paragraph.
3) Provisioning: upon countersignature, Redwood will begin Dedicated provisioning; expected go-live is T+10 business days for Azure pools (T = signature).

DocuSign link (draft envelope): https://docusign.net/sign/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-NEO-0042

If that summary looks right, Sophie can reply with a quick approval and I’ll kick off the DocuSign. If procurement wants different conversion math, let me know and we’ll run the numbers one more time.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
